title: Updating restaurant hours everywhere, including Google
seoTitle: Updating restaurant hours everywhere, including Google
description: Keep your phone, website, and listings in sync when hours change. Handle holiday updates quickly and avoid confusing guests.
question: How do I update restaurant hours Google and keep my restaurant hours right everywhere?
answer: Start by changing your Google Business Profile hours, then match the same hours on your website, voicemail, delivery apps, and any phone system or forwarding message. Check holiday closures, late-night service, and special hours separately, then call your own restaurant number to confirm what customers hear. If you use ROAL, it can read your public hours and answer callers about them, while questions it cannot answer go to your inbox.
summary: You’ll learn how to update restaurant hours across Google, your phone, and other listings without creating mixed messages.
intro:
Yes — the fastest way to update restaurant hours Google is to change your hours in Google Business Profile first, then copy the same hours everywhere else customers can find you. If the hours do not match, people will still call during the wrong times and get frustrated.

For a restaurant, hours are not just a listing detail. They affect pickup calls, delivery orders, staff load, and how many people show up at the door after close. Keeping them consistent is a small task that saves a lot of awkward calls and wasted time.

sections.h2: Where should your hours match first?
sections.body:
Start with the places customers check before they call. For most independent restaurants, that means Google, your website, your voicemail or phone greeting, and any delivery apps you use.

A simple order of work helps:
- Google Business Profile hours
- Your website header, contact page, and footer
- Holiday hours and special closures
- Your phone greeting or on-hold message
- Delivery apps and online ordering pages

If you run a family restaurant, a pizza shop, or a deli, even one wrong line can create a mess. For example, if Google says you close at 10 p.m. but your website says 9 p.m., you may get callers asking, "Are you still open?" right when your staff is trying to shut down. Put one person in charge of hours changes and make them update every channel the same day.

ROAL helps here because it reads your public hours when you set it up from your website, Google Maps link, or "Name, City." It can also answer callers about hours and address, which cuts down on repeated questions when your team is busy.

sections.h2: How do I update restaurant hours Google the right way?
sections.body: If you have multiple locations, repeat the same process for each one. A guest calling your Hoboken store should not hear Jersey City hours by mistake.

sections.h2: What should your phone greeting say when hours change?
sections.body:
Your phone greeting should be short and useful. Do not overload it. The goal is to answer the main question fast: are you open, and what can I do next?

A good greeting can sound like this:
"Thanks for calling. We’re open today until 9 p.m. For pickup orders, please stay on the line. For holiday hours, check our Google listing or website."

Keep a backup version for special days:
"Thanks for calling. We’re closed today for a private event and will reopen tomorrow at 11 a.m."

Checklist for a clean phone message:
- Says today’s hours clearly
- Mentions if pickup is still available
- Matches Google and the website
- Uses the same time zone and closing time
- Is changed back after the holiday

This matters because many callers never look beyond the phone. If your restaurant is busy, ROAL can answer the phone with the hours you have published and handle questions about address, parking, and the menu. It also takes pickup and delivery orders from the live menu, then sends a clean ticket to the kitchen screen. That is helpful when your staff is cooking and cannot keep repeating the same hours all night.

sections.h2: How do I keep delivery apps, website, and voicemail in sync?
sections.body:
Think of hours as one master list, then copy that same list everywhere. The order below keeps things organized:

| Place | What to check | How often |
|---|---|---|
| Google | Regular and special hours | When hours change |
| Website | Homepage, contact page, footer | When hours change |
| Voicemail / phone greeting | Today’s open-close time | When hours change |
| Delivery apps | Store hours and holiday hours | When hours change |
| In-store sign | Door and counter hours | When hours change |

If you are doing pickup only after 8 p.m., say that plainly. Example: "Kitchen closes at 9 p.m., pickup stops at 8:30 p.m." That helps customers order before the rush instead of calling too late.

Here is a simple process you can repeat every time:
1. Update the primary source.
2. Copy the change to your website.
3. Update your phone greeting.
4. Update delivery apps.
5. Test one call and one web page.

If you use a phone forwarding setup, keep the forwarding message current too. For example, if calls go to another line during busy periods, the caller still needs to hear the right hours before someone picks up. When codes or carrier settings are involved, confirm with your carrier and test with a real call.

sections.h2: What should you do for holidays, storms, and special closures?
sections.body:
Special hours are where most mistakes happen. A restaurant may post regular hours correctly, then forget to change them for Thanksgiving, a snow day, or a private catering event.

Use this quick holiday checklist:
- Set special hours in Google
- Change your voicemail or phone greeting
- Update the website banner or contact page
- Tell staff what callers should hear
- Remove the special message when regular hours return

A worked example helps. Say your normal hours are 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and you plan to close at 4 p.m. on Christmas Eve. Put 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. in the special hours field, then change the greeting to: "We’re open today until 4 p.m. Please place pickup orders before then."

If you are closed all day, say that directly. Do not leave the old hours up and hope customers figure it out. That creates confusion at the host stand and fills the phone with calls you cannot serve.

ROAL is useful for this kind of change because its hours live in the same place as the rest of the phone host setup. If a question comes in that it cannot answer, it goes to your inbox once, and the host learns from that answer going forward. That keeps hours questions from becoming a daily interruption.

sections.h2: How can you check that the new hours really work?
sections.body:
After every hours change, do a real-world check. Do not assume the listing saved correctly just because you clicked publish.

Use this 10-minute test:
1. Search your restaurant on Google.
2. Open the listing and read the hours aloud.
3. Call the main number from a cell phone.
4. Listen to the greeting and note the time mentioned.
5. Check your website on mobile.
6. Ask one employee what hours they think are live.

That last step matters more than people think. If your team gives three different answers, guests will get three different answers too. Put the hours in a shared note or on the prep sheet so everyone uses the same version.

You can also keep a simple change log like this:
| Date | Change | Places updated |
|---|---|---|
| Friday | Close at 8 p.m. for event | Google, website, phone |
| Monday | Back to normal hours | Google, website, phone |

If you want a place to sanity-check your setup, [Build a free test host](/try) from your website or Google Maps link. You can call it right in the browser before going live. That makes it easier to catch a wrong hour before customers do.

takeaways: Keep one master hours list and copy it to Google, your website, voicemail, and delivery apps.
Use special hours for holidays and one-off closures instead of changing your regular schedule.
Test the live phone greeting after every hours update.
Make one person responsible for hours changes so the message stays consistent.

faq.q: How do I update restaurant hours Google quickly?
faq.a: Open your Google Business Profile and edit the regular hours first, then add special hours for holidays or closures. After saving, check the listing on a phone and call your restaurant number to confirm the message matches what you published.

faq.q: Should my website and Google hours always match?
faq.a: Yes. If they do not match, customers may trust the wrong one and show up late or call at the wrong time. Keep one master schedule and update both places on the same day.

faq.q: What should I say on my voicemail when hours change?
faq.a: Say the current open and close time in one short sentence, then mention whether pickup is still available. Keep it direct, like: "We’re open today until 9 p.m. For pickup orders, please stay on the line."

faq.q: How do I handle holiday hours for a restaurant?
faq.a: Set special hours in Google, update your website, and change your phone greeting for the holiday. Then remove or replace the message when normal hours return so customers do not get stale information.
